Emma —

Thanks for the note. Attached is a short packet: 1) a token-mix export for the last 90 days, 2) an internal cost model showing per-token economics by model family, and 3) a one-page ROI case study from a similar ecommerce customer where moving to a reserved pool reduced unit cost by ~27% and reduced p95 latency by ~35ms due to prioritization and KV cache locality.

High-level takeaways:
- Your usage is ~62% generation/chat tokens, ~28% embedding tokens, ~10% rerank/misc. Generation spend is concentrated on long-context search flows (avg 1,400 tokens/session).
- Moving to a 6-month committed tier with a burst buffer and prefix caching pays back within 7–9 weeks on current run rates (we modeled conservative 15% increase in traffic).
- For Opal's critical search path, switching to a dedicated instance family (A100-like reservations) drops median latency by ~22ms vs current shared-hosted routing and reduces cost per 1M generation tokens by ~$310 after quantization and batching.

I've left comments in the spreadsheet (inference_cost_model_OPAL_v3.xlsx) showing the scenarios we ran. Ben has suggested pricing/term options below — Ben, can you confirm the math and add recommended list/discount tiers?

Emma —

Following Camila's analysis: we ran three commit scenarios in the attached workbook. Highlights:
- 12-month commit (tier C) with 20% uplift yields the best blended unit economics and predictable budgeting; estimated annual savings ~23% vs metered.
- 6-month commit + burst credits reduces near-term spend but has slightly higher blended unit cost.
- Dedicated Dedicated+ (reserved GPU pool) option provides the latency SLO you'd need for your real-time search queries; pricing reflects an infra uplift but net savings from batching/quantization still materialize at scale.

Proposed commercial options (brief):
1) 12m Tier C: 2.5B gen tokens + 500M embed tokens, 10% discount off list + 60% net-of-effort uplift credit in month 1 for migration.
2) 6m Tier B: 1.4B gen + 250M embed, 5% discount, includes 200k burst tokens.
3) Dedicated+ Pilot: 3-month pilot with committed baseline and assessed SLA of p95 < 160ms on the search path; pricing by capacity node.

Marissa, Emma — if you want, we can bake a short exec memo that shows the payback timeline and a 90-day migration checklist. I can also surface a limited promotional credit for first-quarter usage if they sign within 30 days of DocuSign.

Attachments: inference_cost_model_OPAL_v3.xlsx

Best,

- Operational case: Dedicated+ pilot for the search path will improve p95 latency and reduce tail variance (important for live search UX). We recommend a 90-day migration window with a guarded rollback and a one-week canary to validate prompt-level quality regressions.

Commercial ask: To accelerate the deal and align with Opal's procurement cycles, we can offer a one-time 8% signing credit on the first 3 months of committed usage (applies to Tier C). This is a limited offer tied to a DocuSign within 30 days.
